text:
sam: Heads up — after the window_threshold tweak at 08:10 we saw a latency spike on prod continuous-batcher for short requests :grimacing:

maria: :eyes: saw the alert. which hosts/queues?

sam: us-east cluster c-3, q=low_latency. 99p went from ~50ms -> ~350ms for small reqs. throughput down ~12%.

nate: link to graphs: https://grafana.redwood/prod/d/xyz/continuous-batcher?from=now-1h :point_up:

aj: quick flame/profile shows microbatch sizes collapsed to 1 more often, and kernel chooser flipped to fallback matmul path when batch_shape=(1,64)

maria: hmm kernel routing flip + KV cache miss storms?

sam: logs show KV miss ratio doubled during spike. also many tiny batches queued up hitting prefetch lock contention.

aj: looked at the heuristic change:
```
# before
window_threshold=0.12
# after
window_threshold=0.06
```
We tightened wait window — emits earlier => less coalescing.

nate: so policy created more aggressive early-emit, starving coalescing. small batches pick a different kernel -> worse per-token perf.

maria: propose revert threshold to previous value and run canary on dedicated pool immediately.

sam: rolling back threshold now on us-east-c-3. also can we increase token_budget_target for low_latency route to avoid kernel switch on 1-token batches?

aj: pushing a hotfix: add guard min_batch_size=2 for low_latency and bump token_budget from 32 -> 64; PR #4321

perf-bot: deploy started: canary -> 3 nodes in us-east-c-3. CI passed.

maria: monitoring dashboards for 10m, watching 95/99p

sam: after ~6min canary 99p down to ~60ms, throughput recovered. KV miss back to baseline.

nate: follow-ups: emit batch_shape->kernel histograms, instrument KV prefetch lock hold time with route_id and trace_id.

aj: will open RFC for batcher release gating and auto-rollback on >10% latency regression within 15m of deploy.

maria: nice triage. add this to postmortem if we don't revert prod config change in config repo.

sam: thanks all :thumbsup:
